lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the effect of dilation on lines through and off the center
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: the effect of dilation on lines through and off the center

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: These two examples show the same idea in two different formats.

items.prompt: Two triangles share two pairs of equal angles. Similar?

steps: The third angles must match too.

items.prompt: What happens to a line through the centre of dilation?

steps: Every point stays on the ray from the centre.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Dilate the point (4, 3) about the origin with scale factor 3. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 12 becomes a side of length 48. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 1/4; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 36; the area is multiplied by 16

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 36° and ∠B = 93°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 36° and ∠E = 93°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that passes through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a line through the origin with a different slope
is mapped to a parallel line a fixed distance away
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped onto itself

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-2, 5) about the origin with scale factor 3. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 8 becomes a side of length 24. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 3
scale factor 1/3; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 16; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 9

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 55° and ∠B = 37°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 55° and ∠E = 37°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a line with slope multiplied by the scale factor
is mapped to a parallel line
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped onto itself

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-4, -4) about the origin with scale factor 5. Give the image.
